For symmetric S, if D_k(S) is the sum of squared k-by-k minors over ordered disjoint row/column sets, then a random physical bipartition obeys E E_k(S[I,J])=4^-k D_k(S), hence some cut loses only the universal sqrt(2) factor in the half-Riesz density bound.
If max s_j(B)^2 <= rho ||B||_F^2 with rho<1/3, then E_3(B)>=(1-3rho)||B||_F^6/6 and the square-assisted density bound is <=11.425362339386691 (1-3rho)^-1/12 |a|^-1/2 ||B||_F^-1/2.
